items.title_en: September PPI runs double the forecast (+1.3% m/m, 6.3% y/y), retail sales +0.8% – gold dips for five minutes, then pops to 4,167
items.summary_en: BLS (8:30 AM ET): September PPI rose 1.3% m/m (est. 0.6%; prior revised to 0.5%) and 6.3% y/y, the biggest monthly and annual gains since 2022. Energy +10.8%, gasoline +20.3%; PPI ex food and energy +0.7% (est. 0.3%), ex food, energy and trade just +0.5%. Census: retail sales +0.8% (est. 0.3%), ex-autos +0.9% (est. 0.6%), but ex autos and gas only +0.25% after about 1.1% in August. CME FedWatch (via CNBC): October hike odds near 34%, up from under 18% a week ago. Spot gold (CNBC XAU=): 4,149.80 at the print, a 4,138.10 low within five minutes, a 4,167.10 high at 9:15 AM ET, and 4,156.20 at 9:30 AM ET.
items.reason_en: Near term: hot data 'should' hit gold, but with energy doing most of the PPI damage and non-gas spending slowing, bonds caught a bid and yields fell, so gold bounced. If yields turn back up, that bounce is at risk. Longer term: 6.3% producer inflation tends to filter into consumer prices, which gives the Fed cover to hike again at the Oct. 27–28 meeting and keeps pressure on gold; the Iran war both feeds inflation and keeps haven demand alive.

items.summary_en: CNBC (Reuters): spot gold rose 1.3% to $4,158.63/oz at 10:57 PM ET, rebounding from Wednesday's lowest level since Oct 7; December futures gained 1.8% to $4,180. items.reason_en: Near term: a relief bounce as the dollar and yields unwind part of the CPI overshoot, but gold has only retraced about half of Wednesday's drop and is stalling below $4,160. The 8:30 AM ET PPI and retail sales prints are the test; hot numbers could send it back toward $4,100 and lower. Longer term: central bank buying and haven demand (Iran, fiscal worries) still underpin bullion, but as long as the Fed leans toward more hikes, a durable uptrend is hard to rebuild.

items.summary_en: investingLive (Asia wrap, 11:22 PM ET): Treasuries extended their rebound, taking the 10-year yield 21 bp below the high it hit after Wednesday's CPI; the dollar fell against most majors and gold rallied about $40. A Bloomberg report that China may hold more U.S. debt than official data show, parked with custodians outside the U.S., added support; Canada's reported holdings of U.S. securities have climbed to nearly $600 billion. The report is unconfirmed. Yahoo Finance had the dollar index (DX-Y.NYB) at about 102.09 at 2:00 AM ET versus a 102.55 prior close.
items.reason_en: Near term: lower yields cut the opportunity cost of holding gold and a softer dollar adds fuel, so the bounce has a tailwind as long as yields keep drifting lower; a DXY break below 102 in New York would confirm it. Medium term: if China really is still holding Treasuries quietly, worries about fading foreign demand ease, which caps long-end yields but also takes some air out of the de-dollarization story that has supported gold.

items.title_en: Hormuz heats up: Singapore-flagged boxship sunk, IRGC 'counting the moments' to hit U.S. warships – reports Iran is evacuating bases
items.summary_en: CNBC Daily Open (9:35 PM ET Oct 14): the Singapore-registered container ship GFS Pride was hit by an unidentified projectile, caught fire and sank in the Strait of Hormuz; all 21 crew were evacuated safely. A second vessel, GFS Giselle, took hull damage but reached safe anchorage. Singapore's maritime authority called the attacks a breach of international law. Tehran said it is 'counting the moments' until it can strike U.S. warships, while CENTCOM said U.S. and partner forces clearly control the strait. investingLive (8:40 PM ET Oct 14): unconfirmed reports say the IRGC ordered several military bases evacuated, and Iranian officials reportedly told regional diplomats they are '100% certain' a U.S. strike is coming.
items.reason_en: Near term: rising U.S.–Iran escalation risk supports haven demand, especially if the evacuation reports are confirmed or a strike actually lands. The oil channel cuts the other way by feeding inflation and Fed hike bets, so gold benefits most when war headlines hit as a surprise. Longer term: a drawn-out conflict (the IMF now assumes Hormuz reopens only in March 2027) keeps a floor under haven and central bank demand.

items.summary_en: investingLive (citing an exclusive Reuters interview, 5:44 PM ET Oct 14): San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said further rate increases are more likely than not, but she is still weighing timing and sees no need to act at the Oct 27–28 meeting. She said gasoline is driving headline inflation while core remains sticky, upside inflation risks stay elevated, and a stable labor market lets the Fed focus on prices. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee called the CPI data discouraging, and the Beige Book flagged intensifying, diesel-driven price pressure. Investing.com notes Chair Kevin Warsh speaks late Thursday New York time at the IMF meetings in Bangkok, before the Fed's blackout begins Saturday.
items.reason_en: Near term: Daly takes some air out of an October hike (a small plus for gold) but confirms the tightening bias, firming up a December move – a net negative. Warsh is the next big event risk after PPI and retail sales. Longer term: 'higher for longer' keeps real yields positive, the main headwind for bullion.

items.title: Tên lửa Houthi trúng tòa nhà trụ sở Saudi Aramco ở Dhahran sau khi Ả Rập Xê Út không kích Sanaa – Brent đầu phiên Á nhích lên ~106,4 USD
items.summary: Reuters: Bộ Năng lượng Ả Rập Xê Út xác nhận một tòa nhà hành chính của Aramco ở Dhahran bị tấn công tối thứ Ba 13/10 (giờ Ả Rập Xê Út, ≈ rạng sáng 14/10 giờ VN), gây cháy hạn chế, không có thương vong. Nguồn tin công ty nói một tên lửa đạn đạo đánh trúng tòa văn phòng, hư hại 3 tầng trên cùng. Trước đó liên quân do Ả Rập Xê Út dẫn đầu không kích kho nhiên liệu Sabah ngoại ô Sanaa (Yemen); Houthi đe dọa cả trụ sở Aramco và một nhà máy lọc dầu ở Riyadh. Tên lửa bị đánh chặn rơi mảnh xuống Riyadh làm 4 người bị thương. Ông Trump đã điện đàm với Thái tử Mohammed bin Salman; Mỹ đến nay vẫn chưa tham chiến trực tiếp. Eo Hormuz vẫn bị Iran đóng từ tháng 2 nên tuyến Bab el-Mandeb càng quan trọng. Thị trường: Brent (BZ=F, Yahoo) 106,39 USD lúc 06:45 VN 14/10, so với giá chốt 105,69; vàng COMEX GC=F gần như đi ngang quanh 4.179–4.184 USD (05:00–06:45 VN). CNBC chưa có bài về vụ tấn công Aramco.
items.reason: Ngắn hạn: rủi ro địa chính trị là lực đỡ trú ẩn cho vàng, nhưng tác động lớn hơn là qua dầu: dầu cao → lạm phát → Fed thêm lý do tăng lãi → USD/lợi suất mạnh → bất lợi vàng. Hai lực trái chiều nên vàng gần như đứng yên sáng nay. Trung – dài hạn: nếu Houthi đánh tiếp cơ sở dầu của Ả Rập Xê Út, giá dầu có thể tăng mạnh và kéo kỳ vọng tăng lãi lên; nếu Mỹ/Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ can thiệp làm leo thang chiến sự, cầu trú ẩn vào vàng sẽ rõ hơn.

items.title_en: Houthi missile hits Saudi Aramco HQ building in Dhahran after Saudi strikes on Sanaa – Brent edges up to ~$106.40 in Asia
items.summary_en: Reuters: Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry confirmed an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran was hit Tuesday evening (Saudi time), causing a limited fire and no casualties. A company source said a ballistic missile struck the office tower, damaging the top three floors. Earlier, the Saudi-led coalition hit the Sabah fuel depot outside Sanaa, Yemen; the Houthis threatened both Aramco's headquarters and a Riyadh refinery. Debris from an intercepted missile injured four people in Riyadh. President Trump spoke with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman; the US has not joined the fighting directly. Iran has kept the Strait of Hormuz closed since February, which makes the Bab el-Mandeb route even more important. Markets: Brent (BZ=F, Yahoo) $106.39 at 7:45 PM ET Oct 13 vs. a $105.69 settle; COMEX gold (GC=F) flat around $4,179–4,184 (6:00–7:45 PM ET). No CNBC story on the Aramco attack yet.
items.reason_en: Near term: geopolitical risk is a safe-haven tailwind for gold, but the bigger effect runs through oil – higher crude → hotter inflation → more reason for the Fed to hike → firmer dollar and yields → headwind for gold. The two forces offset, so gold barely moved overnight. Bigger picture: if the Houthis keep hitting Saudi oil infrastructure, crude can spike and pull rate-hike bets higher; if the US or Turkey gets drawn in and the war escalates, the safe-haven bid for gold should become clearer.

items.summary: Bloomberg (qua Oninvest) và Kitco (đăng 15:37 UTC 13/10 = 22:37 VN): Phó Thống đốc NHTW Kazakhstan Aliya Moldabekova nói lợi suất trái phiếu Mỹ cao nhất 24 năm khiến USD hấp dẫn hơn và giảm sức hút của vàng; vàng đã chiếm khoảng 78% dự trữ ngoại hối (386 tấn, dự trữ 66,4 tỷ USD cuối tháng 9), 'giống danh mục một tài sản'. Mục tiêu giảm về 75% trước cuối năm, một nửa bằng bán quyền chọn và một nửa bán vàng vật chất (báo Kazakhstan ước khoảng 12 tấn, ~1,6 tỷ USD). Nếu vàng dưới 4.000 USD, tỷ trọng có thể tự giảm về mục tiêu.
items.reason: Ngắn hạn: tin xấu về tâm lý vì NHTW mua vàng là trụ cột của đà tăng nhiều năm; khối lượng ~12 tấn không lớn nhưng tạo nguồn cung bán quanh vùng giá hiện tại. Trung – dài hạn: nếu thêm NHTW khác tái cân bằng khi lợi suất Mỹ cao, lực đỡ từ cầu chính phủ yếu đi; ngược lại Trung Quốc vẫn mua 23 tháng liên tiếp, nên chưa phải xu hướng chung. Mốc 4.000 USD là vùng cần theo dõi.

items.title_en: Kazakhstan flips from buyer to seller: cutting gold to 75% of reserves from 78% by end-2026
items.summary_en: Bloomberg (via Oninvest) and Kitco (posted 11:37 AM ET Oct 13): Kazakhstan central bank Deputy Governor Aliya Moldabekova said 24-year-high Treasury yields make the dollar more attractive and gold less so; gold already makes up about 78% of FX reserves (386 tonnes, $66.4B in reserves at end-September) – 'like a single-asset portfolio'. The target is 75% by year-end, half via selling options and half via physical sales (local press estimates roughly 12 tonnes, ~$1.6B). If gold drops below $4,000, the share could fall to target on its own.
items.reason_en: Near term: bad for sentiment, since central-bank buying has been a pillar of the multi-year rally; ~12 tonnes isn't large, but it adds supply around current prices. Bigger picture: if other central banks rebalance while US yields are high, official-sector support weakens; on the other hand China has bought 23 months in a row, so it's not a broad trend yet. $4,000 is the level to watch.

items.summary_en: Boston Fed President Susan Collins spoke 4:00–4:45 PM ET Oct 13 at the Boston Fed's regional banking conference. Reuters (4:01 PM ET): she backed September's hike to 3.75–4.00% and now thinks 'it would be appropriate to raise rates somewhat further before year-end to ensure inflation returns to the 2% target in a timely and sustainable way'. Timing depends on incoming data. She was upbeat on GDP growth and a labor market near full employment, but warned headline and core inflation will run above 2% for the next few months on refined fuels (jet, diesel, heating oil), AI investment, tariffs and the Middle East war. No same-day CNBC story; the full text wasn't on the Boston Fed site yet. items.reason_en: Clearly hawkish: Collins confirmed one more hike before end-2026 (the market leans December over the Oct 27–28 meeting). In theory, more Fed tightening plus high yields is bearish for gold near term – and in practice GC=F fell about $5–8 (4,186 → ~4,181) within 20–40 minutes of her start. Bigger picture: if today's 8:30 AM ET CPI runs hot, December hike odds climb and gold stays under pressure; if CPI is soft, her remarks matter less since she doesn't vote this year.

items.summary_en: Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin (non-voter this year, votes in 2027) began speaking at 1:00 PM ET Oct 13. Two headlines (FinancialJuice, Newsquawk): 1:16 PM ET '2% inflation is not some unicorn, it's something we can achieve'; 1:44 PM ET 'we can see the impact of AI investment on US inflation'. As of 1:53 PM ET there was no CNBC or Reuters story and no speech text on the Richmond Fed site. Gold reaction (COMEX GC=F, Yahoo, 5-min bars, ET): 10:15 AM 4,193.0 · 12:45 PM 4,180.1 · 1:00 PM (start) 4,175.9 · 1:15 PM 4,180.1 · 1:25 PM low 4,176.1 · 1:43 PM 4,179.7. items.reason_en: Slightly hawkish but no new rate signal: Barkin stressed the commitment to 2% and said AI is pushing inflation up, consistent with the 'may need to hike more' stance he laid out Sep 22. In theory a mild negative for gold, but in practice gold moved only about $4 (4,176–4,180) and the dollar and yields barely budged – he doesn't vote and the market is waiting on Wednesday's 8:30 AM ET CPI. The selling came before the speech (4,193 at 10:15 AM → 4,176 at 1:00 PM ET). Bigger picture: a Fed committed to 2% with the 10-year above 5.2% remains a headwind; a hot CPI would firm up December hike bets.

items.summary: CNBC: BlackRock (quản lý hơn 15.300 tỷ USD) nâng khuyến nghị trái phiếu Chính phủ Mỹ lên overweight, hạ cổ phiếu Mỹ về trung lập. Hãng cho rằng kỳ vọng Fed tăng thêm 160 điểm cơ bản trong 12 tháng tới là 'quá đà', ưu tiên trái phiếu ngắn hạn. Lợi suất 10 năm Mỹ đã tăng khoảng 110 điểm cơ bản từ đầu năm lên quanh 5,25%, phần lớn do giá năng lượng cao vì xung đột Trung Đông.
items.reason: Nếu dòng tiền lớn quay lại mua trái phiếu và kỳ vọng Fed thắt chặt hạ nhiệt, lợi suất có thể đã gần đỉnh → giảm chi phí cơ hội nắm giữ vàng, hỗ trợ vàng trung – dài hạn. Ngắn hạn đây mới là quan điểm, chưa thay đổi lộ trình Fed; CPI tuần này vẫn quyết định.

items.title_en: BlackRock goes overweight Treasuries for the first time in ~6 years, says markets overprice Fed tightening
items.summary_en: CNBC: BlackRock (over $15.3 trillion AUM) upgraded US Treasuries to overweight and cut US equities to neutral. The firm called expectations for another 160 bps of Fed hikes over the next 12 months 'overdone' and favors the short end. The 10-year yield is up about 110 bps year-to-date to around 5.25%, largely on high energy prices from the Middle East conflict.
items.reason_en: If big money rotates back into bonds and Fed-tightening bets cool, yields may be near a peak → lower opportunity cost for gold, supportive over the medium to long term. Near term it's just a view and doesn't change the Fed path; this week's CPI still decides.

items.title: IMF cảnh báo lợi suất trái phiếu chính phủ có thể tăng vọt 'mất trật tự' vì nợ công, lạm phát và vay nợ AI
items.summary: CNBC: Báo cáo Ổn định Tài chính Toàn cầu (GFSR) của IMF công bố 13/10 tại Bangkok cảnh báo nợ kỷ lục khiến thị trường trái phiếu 'dễ tổn thương trước các cú sốc tài khóa và lạm phát'; tỷ trọng nắm giữ trái phiếu Mỹ của quỹ phòng hộ tăng lên khoảng 9% (2025) từ 4% (2022), có nguy cơ 'tháo chạy mất trật tự'. Các hyperscaler AI chiếm 10% lượng phát hành trái phiếu hạng đầu tư toàn cầu (từ dưới 1% năm 2024), cạnh tranh vốn với trái phiếu chính phủ.
items.reason: Ngắn hạn: lợi suất tăng vọt gây áp lực lên vàng (chi phí cơ hội cao, USD mạnh) và có thể kéo theo bán tháo tài sản để lấy thanh khoản. Dài hạn: rủi ro nợ công và niềm tin vào trái phiếu chính phủ suy giảm là lý do cốt lõi để ngân hàng trung ương và nhà đầu tư giữ vàng làm tài sản an toàn.

items.title_en: IMF warns sovereign yields could spike in a 'disorderly' way on public debt, inflation and AI borrowing
items.summary_en: CNBC: the IMF's Global Financial Stability Report, released Oct 13 in Bangkok, warned record debt leaves bond markets 'vulnerable to fiscal and inflation shocks'; hedge funds' share of Treasury holdings rose to about 9% (2025) from 4% (2022), raising the risk of a 'disorderly unwind'. AI hyperscalers now account for 10% of global investment-grade bond issuance (from under 1% in 2024), competing with governments for capital.
items.reason_en: Near term: a yield spike pressures gold (higher opportunity cost, stronger dollar) and can trigger selling of assets to raise cash. Bigger picture: public-debt risk and eroding trust in government bonds are core reasons central banks and investors hold gold as a safe asset.

items.title_en: China buys gold for a 23rd straight month: about 23 tonnes added in September
items.summary_en: Reuters: the People's Bank of China's gold reserves rose to 77.47M oz at end-September from 76.73M oz at end-August – an addition of 740,000 oz (≈ 23 tonnes), more than in August – extending the buying streak to 23 months.
